test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jul 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: R’s weighing machine shows 400 gm when the actual weight is 350 gm. The cost price of almonds is ₹880 per kg and packets of 200 gm are made using the faulty machine. What should be the selling price (in ₹) of each packet to get a profit of 25%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight Ratio (Actual : Faulty) = 350 : 400 = 7 : 8

Actual weight of 200 gm packet = 200 × (7/8) = 175 gm

CP of 1000 gm = ₹880 ⇒ CP of 175 gm = 880 × (175/1000) = ₹154

SP for 25% profit = 154 × 1.25 = ₹192.5

**∴ The correct answer is 192.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Actual weight = 350 gm | Machine weight = 400 gm

CP of almonds = ₹880 per kg (1000 gm)

Packet size (as per machine) = 200 gm

Desired profit = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Actual Weight = (Actual Reading ÷ Faulty Reading) × Given Reading

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 
 Machine Reading: 400 gm
 → Actual: 350 gm
 
 
• 
 
 
 Packet: 200 gm
 → Actual: 175 gm
 
 CP of 175 gm = ₹154
 SP (25% Profit) = ₹192.5

**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual weight in a 200 gm packet = (350 ÷ 400) × 200

⇒ Actual weight = 0.875 × 200 = 175 gm

⇒ CP of 1 gm = 880 ÷ 1000 = ₹0.88

⇒ CP of 175 gm = 175 × 0.88 = ₹154

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 154 × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ SP = 154 × 1.25

⇒ SP = ₹192.5

**∴ The correct answer is 192.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Profit Percentage

Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100, where error is the difference between actual and faulty weight.

Profit and Loss Relation with SP/CP

Profit = SP − CP. If Profit% is given, SP = CP × [ (100 + P%) ÷ 100 ].

Effective Profit with Faulty Weights

Total Profit Multiplier = (Faulty Weight ÷ Actual Weight) × (1 + Profit%).
